source: platform/experiments/INDEX.json + the record JSONs it lists (read at export time) and platform/DATASET_REGISTRY.md (dataset facts transcribed in platform_export.py). No placeholder numbers.

datasets.name: C-MAPSS FD001 — Turbofan Degradation
datasets.licence: NASA research use; formal licence text not confirmed
datasets.note: 1 operating condition, 1 fault mode (HPC). Train 20,631 rows / 100 engines. The original PREDICAI system (LSTM → ONNX → Rust API) serves this subset.

datasets.name: C-MAPSS FD002 — Turbofan Degradation
datasets.licence: NASA research use; formal licence text not confirmed
datasets.note: 6 operating conditions, 1 fault mode. Train 53,759 rows / 260 engines; 23 features after derivation.

datasets.name: C-MAPSS FD003 — Turbofan Degradation
datasets.licence: NASA research use; formal licence text not confirmed
datasets.note: 1 operating condition, 2 fault modes (HPC + fan). Train 24,720 rows / 100 engines; 15 features (sensor_6 kept, unlike FD001).

datasets.name: C-MAPSS FD004 — Turbofan Degradation
datasets.licence: NASA research use; formal licence text not confirmed
datasets.note: 6 operating conditions, 2 fault modes. Train 61,249 rows / 249 engines. On FD004 the LSTM wins RMSE/MAE but loses the NASA score to Ridge — recorded as measured.

datasets.name: AI4I 2020 Predictive Maintenance
datasets.note: 10,000 × 14; binary machine-failure label (339 failures, ≈3.4%). Data is SYNTHETIC (rule-generated failures) — the 5 failure-mode flags define the target and are declared leakage columns, never features.

datasets.name: SECOM Manufacturing
datasets.note: 1,567 rows × 590 anonymised sensor columns; 104 fails (≈6.6%). Heavy missingness → 450 features survive the wave-1 pipeline. Features are anonymised — explanations cite sensor indices only.

datasets.name: CWRU Bearing
datasets.note: Drive-end vibration at 12 kHz; Normal / InnerRace / Ball / OuterRace. Fault DIAGNOSIS of seeded faults, not prediction. Headline result is the recording-wise evaluation (accuracy 0.665) — see Research view.

datasets.name: Paderborn Bearing
datasets.note: Integrated scope: 3 of 32 bearings (K001 healthy, KA01 outer-race, KI01 inner-race) → 30,022 windows. Non-commercial licence. One physical bearing per class — no unseen-bearing generalisation claim.

datasets.name: IMS Bearing (Run-to-Failure)
datasets.note: Test 1 integrated (wave 5, after the user approved the 1.08 GB download): 2,156 snapshots × 8 channels at 20 kHz. Teardown ground truth: bearing 3 inner-race + bearing 4 roller defects. No per-snapshot labels — evaluation is alarm timing only.

datasets.name: NASA Li-ion Battery Aging
datasets.note: 4 room-temperature run-to-failure batteries (B0005/6/7/18), 636 discharge-cycle rows. EOL = capacity < 1.4 Ah; B0007 never crosses (censored) and is excluded from LOBO scoring.

datasets.name: FEMTO-ST / PRONOSTIA Bearing
datasets.note: 17 run-to-failure bearings (IEEE PHM 2012). Researched-only: ingestion effort (thousands of small CSVs) and mirror provenance pinning put it behind current priorities.

datasets.name: XJTU-SY Bearing
datasets.note: 15 run-to-failure bearings, ≈4.4 GB. Researched-only: mirror-only distribution (provenance risk) and unstated licence.

datasets.name: MFPT Bearing Fault Data
datasets.note: BLOCKED — the official site is gone: mfpt.org redirects domain-wide to ASNT, which offers no dataset, download or licence. No unofficial mirror was substituted.

datasets.name: MIMII Industrial Machine Sound
datasets.note: Researched-only BY DECISION: 100.2 GB of audio (12 zips) is disproportionate to the platform's current stage. A future wave could take one machine type at one SNR (≈7–11 GB).

datasets.name: Bosch Production Line Performance
datasets.note: BLOCKED — no direct download exists; access requires a Kaggle account and acceptance of competition rules (≈14.3 GB, 4,264 anonymised features, ≈0.58% failures).

datasets.name: Milling Tool Wear
datasets.licence: NASA portal; formal licence text not confirmed
datasets.note: 167 milling runs; label = measured flank wear VB (mm). Some runs have missing VB and a few are flagged corrupted in the dataset's own notes — to be excluded and documented, never silently repaired.

datasets.name: Hydraulic Condition Monitoring
datasets.note: 2,205 cycles × 17 sensors; multi-output graded condition classes (cooler / valve / pump leakage / accumulator) — condition grades, not failure events. Not run-to-failure.

datasets.name: MetroPT-3 (Lisbon Metro APU)
datasets.note: 1,516,948 rows × 15 features, Jan–Aug 2020. Ground truth = timestamped maintenance reports only, no per-row labels — evaluation must be event-based.

datasets.name: Automotive Engine Health
datasets.note: No verified public sensor/time-series automotive engine-health dataset with a clear licence was found (searched 2026-11-15). The category is recorded as unfilled rather than inventing an entry.

datasets.name: Motor Electrical Faults (candidates)
datasets.note: No single canonical dataset. Licence-verified candidates researched: UCI Sensorless Drive Diagnosis (CC BY 4.0), KAIST PMSM stator faults (CC BY 4.0), UOEMD-VAFCVS (CC BY 4.0), NLN-EMP (CC0). None downloaded yet.

experiments.protocol: RECORDING-WISE leave-one-recording-out (LeaveOneGroupOut over 12 recordings; groups = recording id): in every fold the held-out recording's windows are the test set and NO window from that recording appears in training. Metrics are computed on the pooled out-of-fold predictions.
experiments.notes: The leakage-safe counterpart of the wave-2 CWRU record. Wave 2 split WINDOWS of 4 recordings (one per class) stratified 80/20, so every test window's recording was also in training — its accuracy/F1 of 1.000 measures within-recording separability only. Here, 12 recordings (3 per class: Normal at 0/1/2 hp; InnerRace/Ball/OuterRace at 0.007/0.014/0.021 inch, 0 hp) are evaluated leave-one-recording-out, so the score below is the first CWRU number in this project that speaks about unseen recordings. It still does NOT cover unseen fault diameters combined with unseen loads jointly, nor different machines. Data note: 99.mat as served by the official host bundles the X098 variable alongside X099; the self-identified X099_DE_time series (2 hp normal) is the one used.

experiments.protocol: LEAVE-ONE-BATTERY-OUT (LOBO): each of B0005, B0006, B0018 is held out in turn and predicted by a model fitted on the other two batteries only; no cycle of the test battery is in training. B0007 is EXCLUDED: it is censored — its capacity never crosses the 1.4 Ah end-of-life threshold (last recorded 1.432 Ah), so it has no observed EOL label.
experiments.notes: Real laboratory battery-aging data (NASA Ames PCoE, Saha & Goebel 2007). LOBO over 3 batteries is a small-sample evaluation: per-battery numbers are reported individually, not hidden in the pooled score.

experiments.protocol: MEASUREMENT-GROUPED split: GroupShuffleSplit by source_file (measurement id), 80/20, seed 42 — no measurement file contributes windows to both sides. NOTE: there is only ONE physical bearing per class in this scope, so train and test still share bearings (different measurements of them).
experiments.notes: Caveat (binding): one physical bearing per class (K001 healthy, KA01 outer-race EDM, KI01 inner-race EDM). The measurement-grouped split removes the window-level leakage of a naive split, but the score measures within-bearing separability across measurements and operating conditions — NOT generalisation to unseen bearings. CC BY-NC 4.0 data: non-commercial use only. real test-rig recordings; KA01/KI01 damage is artificially EDM-seeded in this scope (the full dataset also contains real fatigue damage, not integrated here)

experiments.protocol: zero-shot cross-dataset transfer: wave-4 FD003 CNN-LSTM applied to the official FD001 test set, last window per engine; FD001 data used for scoring only
experiments.notes: Zero-shot FD003 -> FD001 transfer, the mirror of wave 2's FD001 -> FD003 (RMSE 48.80). Asymmetry is expected and is itself the finding: the FD003 model was trained on TWO fault modes (HPC + fan) and a feature set that keeps sensor_6, while FD001 contains only the HPC mode — transferring INTO the narrower domain is not the same problem as transferring out of it. train_s = 0.0 because no training was performed in this run.

experiments.protocol: zero-shot cross-subset transfer: FD002 Ridge (refit, identical config) applied to the official FD004 test set, last window per engine; FD004 data used for scoring only
experiments.notes: Zero-shot FD002 -> FD004 Ridge transfer. Both subsets have six operating conditions; FD002 has 1 fault mode(s), FD004 has 2. The shared 23-feature space makes this the cleanest C-MAPSS transfer pair in the platform; any degradation is therefore attributable to distribution / fault-mode shift, not to feature misalignment. train_s is the deterministic refit time on the source subset.

experiments.protocol: zero-shot cross-dataset transfer: Random Forest trained on all cwru windows, tested on all paderborn windows; label set restricted to the shared ['Normal', 'InnerRace', 'OuterRace']
experiments.notes: Zero-shot cwru -> paderborn bearing-fault transfer. Known shift factors, all documented rather than corrected: sampling rate 12 kHz (CWRU) vs 64 kHz (Paderborn) so identical 2048-sample windows cover 170.7 ms vs 32.0 ms of shaft rotation; different test rigs, bearing geometries, sensor mounting and load/speed regimes; CWRU faults are EDM-seeded single-point defects, Paderborn's are EDM/drilling/engraving defects on a different bearing type. Time-domain statistics (RMS, kurtosis, ...) are amplitude- and rate-sensitive, so degradation vs the in-domain references is the expected result — this record measures it instead of assuming it.

experiments.protocol: EXPLANATION MODEL — deliberately NOT the wave-4 leave-one-battery-out protocol: the forest is fitted on every cycle of B0005, B0006 and B0018 so the attributions describe the fullest model of the three EOL batteries. Its metrics below are IN-SAMPLE and must not be quoted as generalisation — the honest generalisation estimate is the wave-4 LOBO record (pooled RMSE 9.27).
experiments.notes: Explainability record (wave 6): SHAP TreeExplainer attributions of the all-batteries Random Forest for B0005's discharge cycles, on the RUL (cycles) output scale. Attributions describe what THIS model uses — dominated, expectedly, by the capacity trajectory features — not a physical ageing mechanism. The LOBO record remains the performance reference for this dataset.

experiments.protocol: MEASUREMENT-GROUPED split identical to wave 4: GroupShuffleSplit by source_file, 80/20, seed 42; importance measured on the held-out measurements only

The refit reproduces the wave-4 model (same config, split and seed), so the importances belong to that scored model. Caveat carried from wave 4: one physical bearing per class — importances describe within-scope separability, not unseen bearings.

experiments.protocol: TEMPORAL split within one run-to-failure test: each bearing's detector is fitted ONLY on the first 30% of snapshots (early life, nominal by construction) and scored over the full run. No random splitting anywhere — snapshot order is the run's chronology.
experiments.notes: IMS Test 1 integrated in wave 5 after the user approved the 1.08 GB official download that wave 3's size gate had blocked. Detectors see only their own bearing's channels. A sustained alarm on bearings 3/4 late in the run, with bearings 1/2 quiet or much later, is the success pattern this design can honestly show; whatever the measured pattern is, it is reported as measured in EXPERIMENTS_REPORT.md. Data is real run-to-failure rig data (not field data); licence not stated on the PCoE page.

experiments.protocol: RECORDING-WISE leave-one-recording-out (LeaveOneGroupOut over the SAME 12 recordings as wave 4; groups = recording id): in every fold the held-out recording's windows are the test set and NO window from that recording appears in training. experiments.notes: Wave-9 counterpart of the wave-4 recording-wise record: identical protocol, recordings, model and seed; the only change is the feature set (10 time-domain -> 24 combined time + spectral/envelope). experiments.notes: Zero-shot cwru -> paderborn bearing-fault transfer with the wave-9 combined spectral feature set — the wave-5 transfer re-run with the feature set as the only changed variable. The wave-5 time-domain baseline for this direction is carried in extra.wave5_time_domain_baseline; the result is reported as measured, whether or not it improves.

transfers.protocol: zero-shot cross-dataset transfer: wave-4 FD003 CNN-LSTM applied to the official FD001 test set, last window per engine; FD001 data used for scoring only
transfers.notes: Zero-shot FD003 -> FD001 transfer, the mirror of wave 2's FD001 -> FD003 (RMSE 48.80). Asymmetry is expected and is itself the finding: the FD003 model was trained on TWO fault modes (HPC + fan) and a feature set that keeps sensor_6, while FD001 contains only the HPC mode — transferring INTO the narrower domain is not the same problem as transferring out of it. train_s = 0.0 because no training was performed in this run.
transfers.verdict: Near in-domain — RMSE 15.82 vs 13.73 shipped in-domain (+15%). Wide→narrow transfer (2 fault modes → 1) largely works; the reverse direction does not.

transfers.protocol: zero-shot cross-subset transfer: FD002 Ridge (refit, identical config) applied to the official FD004 test set, last window per engine; FD004 data used for scoring only
transfers.notes: Zero-shot FD002 -> FD004 Ridge transfer. Both subsets have six operating conditions; FD002 has 1 fault mode(s), FD004 has 2. The shared 23-feature space makes this the cleanest C-MAPSS transfer pair in the platform; any degradation is therefore attributable to distribution / fault-mode shift, not to feature misalignment. train_s is the deterministic refit time on the source subset.
transfers.verdict: Fails — RMSE 51.38 vs 19.43 in-domain Ridge on FD004 (+165%), despite an identical 23-feature space. The shift is in the distributions / fault modes, not the features.

transfers.protocol: zero-shot cross-subset transfer: FD004 Ridge (refit, identical config) applied to the official FD002 test set, last window per engine; FD002 data used for scoring only
transfers.notes: Zero-shot FD004 -> FD002 Ridge transfer. Both subsets have six operating conditions; FD004 has 2 fault mode(s), FD002 has 1. The shared 23-feature space makes this the cleanest C-MAPSS transfer pair in the platform; any degradation is therefore attributable to distribution / fault-mode shift, not to feature misalignment. train_s is the deterministic refit time on the source subset.
transfers.verdict: Near in-domain — RMSE 18.07 vs 16.58 in-domain Ridge on FD002 (+9%). Again the wide→narrow direction (2 fault modes → 1).

transfers.protocol: zero-shot cross-dataset transfer: Random Forest trained on all cwru windows, tested on all paderborn windows; label set restricted to the shared ['Normal', 'InnerRace', 'OuterRace']
transfers.notes: Zero-shot cwru -> paderborn bearing-fault transfer. Known shift factors, all documented rather than corrected: sampling rate 12 kHz (CWRU) vs 64 kHz (Paderborn) so identical 2048-sample windows cover 170.7 ms vs 32.0 ms of shaft rotation; different test rigs, bearing geometries, sensor mounting and load/speed regimes; CWRU faults are EDM-seeded single-point defects, Paderborn's are EDM/drilling/engraving defects on a different bearing type. Time-domain statistics (RMS, kurtosis, ...) are amplitude- and rate-sensitive, so degradation vs the in-domain references is the expected result — this record measures it instead of assuming it.
transfers.verdict: Fails — accuracy 0.253 vs 0.950 in-domain. The Normal class is never recognised on the target rig (recall 0.0): 'Normal' is rig-specific with time-domain features.

transfers.protocol: zero-shot cross-dataset transfer: Random Forest trained on all paderborn windows, tested on all cwru windows; label set restricted to the shared ['Normal', 'InnerRace', 'OuterRace']
transfers.notes: Zero-shot paderborn -> cwru bearing-fault transfer. Known shift factors, all documented rather than corrected: sampling rate 12 kHz (CWRU) vs 64 kHz (Paderborn) so identical 2048-sample windows cover 170.7 ms vs 32.0 ms of shaft rotation; different test rigs, bearing geometries, sensor mounting and load/speed regimes; CWRU faults are EDM-seeded single-point defects, Paderborn's are EDM/drilling/engraving defects on a different bearing type. Time-domain statistics (RMS, kurtosis, ...) are amplitude- and rate-sensitive, so degradation vs the in-domain references is the expected result — this record measures it instead of assuming it.
transfers.verdict: Fails — accuracy 0.125 vs 0.665 recording-wise in-domain. Normal recall 0.0 again; 12 kHz vs 64 kHz sampling also makes the same 2048-sample window cover 170.7 ms vs 32.0 ms.

transfers.protocol: zero-shot cross-dataset transfer: Random Forest trained on all cwru windows, tested on all paderborn windows; label set restricted to the shared ['Normal', 'InnerRace', 'OuterRace']. Identical to the wave-5 transfer protocol — the ONLY change is the feature set (10 time-domain -> 24 combined).
transfers.notes: Zero-shot cwru -> paderborn bearing-fault transfer with the wave-9 combined spectral feature set — the wave-5 transfer re-run with the feature set as the only changed variable. Shift factors that remain, documented rather than corrected: different test rigs, bearing geometries, sensor mounting and load/speed regimes; shaft-speed-relative defect frequencies are NOT aligned by the rate-free features (sampling rate and shaft speed vary independently); window time spans differ 5.3x. The wave-5 time-domain baseline for this direction is carried in extra.wave5_time_domain_baseline; the result is reported as measured, whether or not it improves.
transfers.verdict: Still fails — accuracy 0.210 vs 0.950 in-domain, slightly WORSE than the time-domain run (0.253). One genuine change: the Normal class is recognised at all now (F1 0.195 vs 0.000). Spectral features did not fix cross-rig transfer.

transfers.protocol: zero-shot cross-dataset transfer: Random Forest trained on all paderborn windows, tested on all cwru windows; label set restricted to the shared ['Normal', 'InnerRace', 'OuterRace']. Identical to the wave-5 transfer protocol — the ONLY change is the feature set (10 time-domain -> 24 combined).
transfers.notes: Zero-shot paderborn -> cwru bearing-fault transfer with the wave-9 combined spectral feature set — the wave-5 transfer re-run with the feature set as the only changed variable. Shift factors that remain, documented rather than corrected: different test rigs, bearing geometries, sensor mounting and load/speed regimes; shaft-speed-relative defect frequencies are NOT aligned by the rate-free features (sampling rate and shaft speed vary independently); window time spans differ 5.3x. The wave-5 time-domain baseline for this direction is carried in extra.wave5_time_domain_baseline; the result is reported as measured, whether or not it improves.
transfers.verdict: Still fails — accuracy 0.187 vs 0.665 recording-wise in-domain, though better than the time-domain run (0.125; F1-macro 0.286 vs 0.156). Normal F1 remains 0.000. Spectral features did not fix cross-rig transfer.

xai.protocol: stratified 80/20, seed 42 (identical to wave-1 AI4I records)
xai.notes: Explainability record (Phase 7): the LightGBM model was retrained with the exact wave-1 config and split so the attributions belong to a real, scored model; `metrics` are that retrained model's test metrics. SHAP values are TreeExplainer attributions for the failure class on the model's raw (log-odds) output scale.

xai.protocol: EXPLANATION MODEL — deliberately NOT the wave-4 leave-one-battery-out protocol: the forest is fitted on every cycle of B0005, B0006 and B0018 so the attributions describe the fullest model of the three EOL batteries. Its metrics below are IN-SAMPLE and must not be quoted as generalisation — the honest generalisation estimate is the wave-4 LOBO record (pooled RMSE 9.27).
xai.notes: Explainability record (wave 6): SHAP TreeExplainer attributions of the all-batteries Random Forest for B0005's discharge cycles, on the RUL (cycles) output scale. Attributions describe what THIS model uses — dominated, expectedly, by the capacity trajectory features — not a physical ageing mechanism. The LOBO record remains the performance reference for this dataset.

xai.protocol: MEASUREMENT-GROUPED split identical to wave 4: GroupShuffleSplit by source_file, 80/20, seed 42; importance measured on the held-out measurements only
xai.notes: Explainability record (wave 6): permutation importance of the wave-4 Paderborn forest, measured as accuracy drop on its grouped test split. The refit reproduces the wave-4 model (same config, split and seed), so the importances belong to that scored model. Caveat carried from wave 4: one physical bearing per class — importances describe within-scope separability, not unseen bearings.

best_results.protocol: RECORDING-WISE leave-one-recording-out (LeaveOneGroupOut over 12 recordings; groups = recording id): in every fold the held-out recording's windows are the test set and NO window from that recording appears in training. Metrics are computed on the pooled out-of-fold predictions.

MEASUREMENT-GROUPED split: GroupShuffleSplit by source_file (measurement id), 80/20, seed 42 — no measurement file contributes windows to both sides. NOTE: there is only ONE physical bearing per class in this scope, so train and test still share bearings (different measurements of them).

MEASUREMENT-GROUPED split: GroupShuffleSplit by source_file (measurement id), 80/20, seed 42 — identical protocol to wave 4; the ONLY change vs wave 4 is the bearing set (real fatigue damage instead of artificial EDM damage). NOTE: one physical bearing per class, so train and test share bearings (different measurements of them).
engine-wise 80/20 train/val (seed 42) + official provided test set, last window per engine — identical to the shipped FD001 LSTM evaluation
engine-wise 80/20 train/val (seed 42) + official provided test set, last window per engine — IDENTICAL to wave 2; the ONLY change vs wave 2 is the normalisation (per-regime sensor scaling)
engine-wise 80/20 train/val (seed 42) + official provided test set, last window per engine
engine-wise 80/20 train/val (seed 42) + official provided test set, last window per engine

LEAVE-ONE-BATTERY-OUT (LOBO): each of B0005, B0006, B0018 is held out in turn and predicted by a model fitted on the other two batteries only; no cycle of the test battery is in training. B0007 is EXCLUDED: it is censored — its capacity never crosses the 1.4 Ah end-of-life threshold (last recorded 1.432 Ah), so it has no observed EOL label.
stratified 80/20, seed 42 (same split as Task A)
